lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 1943, a Harvard chemist armed six sleeping bats with tiny firebombs, while Army cameramen filmed him doing it.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The desert sun woke them up early.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Exactly fifteen minutes later, the barracks caught fire.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Then the control tower went up like a giant candle.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The fire trucks raced to the gate, and the guards refused to open it, because the whole thing was top secret.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: It all started with a dentist, who wrote to the President with a plan to firebomb Japan with bats.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Franklin Roosevelt passed it on with a note. This man is not a nut.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: That's the reference? Not a nut?

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Two years and two million dollars later, the bats finally worked, and the project was cancelled.
